title.zh: 卷一百十四 列傳第一: 后妃一
title.raw: 卷一百十四 列傳第一: 后妃一 Volume 114 Biographies 1: Empresses and Consorts 1

sentences.zh: 后妃一

translations.literal: Empresses and Consorts 1
translations.idiomatic: Empresses and Consorts 1

sentences.zh: 太祖光獻翼聖皇后，名孛兒臺旭真，弘吉剌氏，特薛禪之女也。

translations.literal: The Taizu's Empress Guangxian Yisheng, taboo name Börte Chuju Zhen, of the Kongirat clan, was daughter of Tögüechü.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu's Empress Guangxian Yisheng, whose tabooed name was Börte Chuju Zhen, belonged to the Kongirat clan and was the daughter of Tögüechü.

sentences.zh: 特薛禪與子按陳從太祖征伐有功，賜號國舅，封王爵，以統其部族。

translations.literal: Tögüechü and his son Anchü followed the Taizu on campaigns with merit; they were granted the title Imperial Uncle-in-law, ennobled as kings, to rule their tribe.
translations.idiomatic: Tögüechü and his son Anchü campaigned under the Taizu with distinction; rewarded as imperial uncles-by-marriage and ennobled as kings, they were entrusted to govern their people.

sentences.zh: 有旨：「生女為后，生男尚公主，世世不絕。

translations.literal: There was an edict: "Daughters born shall become empresses; sons born shall marry imperial princesses—generation after generation without end.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "A daughter born to this house shall be made empress; a son born shall marry an imperial princess—so the bond shall never cease from age to age.

sentences.zh: 」世祖至元二年十二月，追謚光獻翼聖皇后。

translations.literal: " In the twelfth month of the second year of Zhiyuan, Shizu posthumously honored her as Empress Guangxian Yisheng.
translations.idiomatic: " In the twelfth month of 1265, Kublai posthumously titled her Empress Guangxian Yisheng.

sentences.zh: 冊文曰：「尊祖宗，致誠孝，實王政之攸先；

translations.literal: The investiture text reads: "To honor the ancestors and fulfill sincere filial piety is truly the foremost of royal government;
translations.idiomatic: The patent of investiture reads: "Revering one's forebears and practicing sincere filial devotion stand foremost among the duties of kingship;

sentences.zh: 法天地，建鴻名，亦母儀之克稱。

translations.literal: To model Heaven and Earth and establish a great name is also what fully befits a mother's exemplar.
translations.idiomatic: to take Heaven and Earth as one's pattern and raise up a great name is likewise what befits the model of a mother to the realm.

sentences.zh: 肆先虔於太室，庸昭示於后昆，體茲至公，節以大惠。

translations.literal: Therefore we first offer reverence in the Grand Chamber and broadly proclaim it to posterity, embodying this supreme fairness and regulating it with great favor.
translations.idiomatic: We therefore offer reverence first in the Grand Chamber and make it known broadly to posterity, embodying this supreme fairness and tempering it with great grace.

sentences.zh: 欽惟光獻皇后，宅收淵靜，稟德柔嘉，當聖神創業之初，有夙夜求賢之助。

translations.literal: Respectfully: Empress Guangxian dwelled in deep stillness and received a gentle, excellent nature; at the beginning when the sacred spirit founded the enterprise, she had the assistance of seeking worthies day and night.
translations.idiomatic: Respectfully considered: Empress Guangxian kept to deep stillness and was endowed with gentle excellence; in the earliest days of the sacred founding she aided the enterprise by seeking worthy men day and night.

sentences.zh: 功施社稷，垂慈訓於景襄；

translations.literal: Her merit extended to the altars of soil and grain; she handed down kindly instruction to Jingxiang;
translations.idiomatic: Her service reached the altars of state; she passed down maternal instruction to Jingxiang;

sentences.zh: 慶衍宮闈，流徽音於莊聖。

translations.literal: Her blessings spread through the inner palace; her fine reputation flowed to Zhuangsheng.
translations.idiomatic: her blessings filled the inner quarters, and her noble fame flowed on to Zhuangsheng.

sentences.zh: 協贊龍飛之運，永詒燕翼之謀。

translations.literal: She assisted the fortune of the dragon's ascent and forever bequeathed the plan of the swallow's wings.
translations.idiomatic: She aided the fortune of the dragon's rise and forever secured the plan by which the dynasty's young would thrive.

sentences.zh: 惟周人著稱《思齊》，亦推本興王之跡；

translations.literal: Only the Zhou people were famed in "Si Qi," also tracing back the traces of the founding king;
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou alone were praised in the "Si Qi," tracing the rise of their founding king to its source;

sentences.zh: 在漢世始謚光烈，蓋篤申追遠之情。

translations.literal: in the Han dynasty they first posthumously titled Guanglie, surely deepening the feeling of honoring the distant past.
translations.idiomatic: in Han they first bestowed the posthumous title Guanglie, deepening the duty of honoring those long departed.

sentences.zh: 是用稽迪舊章，增崇遺美。

translations.literal: Therefore we follow the former regulations and augment the departed excellence.
translations.idiomatic: We therefore follow the ancient statutes and add glory to her departed excellence.

sentences.zh: 謹遣攝太尉某，奉玉冊玉寶，加上尊謚曰光獻翼聖皇后。

translations.literal: We respectfully send the Acting Grand Marshal [name] to present the jade patent and jade seal, adding the honorific posthumous title Empress Guangxian Yisheng.
translations.idiomatic: We respectfully dispatch the Acting Grand Marshal [name] to present the jade patent and jade seal, conferring the honorific posthumous title Empress Guangxian Yisheng.

sentences.zh: 伏惟淑靈降格，典禮備膺，於億萬年，茂隆丕祚。

translations.literal: We humbly hope her virtuous spirit descends; the ritual is fully received—for ten thousand years may her great fortune flourish.
translations.idiomatic: May her virtuous spirit descend; may the rites be fully received—through ten thousand years may her great fortune flourish.

sentences.zh: 」升祔太祖廟。

translations.literal: " She was elevated to accompany the Taizu in the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: " She was enshrined to accompany the Taizu in the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 其餘后妃，有四斡耳朵四十餘人，不記氏族，其名悉見於《表》。

translations.literal: The remaining empresses and consorts in the four ordas numbered more than forty; their clans are not recorded, and their names all appear in the Tables.
translations.idiomatic: His other empresses and consorts in the four ordas numbered more than forty; their clans are not recorded here, and their names all appear in the Tables.

sentences.zh: 后皆仿此。

translations.literal: The empresses below all follow this pattern.
translations.idiomatic: The entries for empresses below follow the same pattern.

sentences.zh: 太宗昭慈皇后，名脫列哥那，乃馬真氏，生定宗。

translations.literal: Taizong's Empress Zhaoci, named Töregene, of the Naiman clan, bore Dingzong.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong's Empress Zhaoci, named Töregene, was of the Naiman clan and bore Güyük.

sentences.zh: 歲辛丑十一月，太宗崩，后稱制攝國者五年。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the xinchou year, Taizong died; the empress ruled as regent for five years.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of 1241 Taizong died, and the empress governed as regent for five years.

sentences.zh: 丙午，會諸王百官，議立定宗。

translations.literal: In the bingwu year she convened the princes and the hundred officials to deliberate on enthroning Dingzong.
translations.idiomatic: In 1246 she convened the princes and officials to decide on enthroning Güyük.

sentences.zh: 朝政多出於后。

translations.literal: Court government mostly issued from the empress.
translations.idiomatic: Most affairs of government issued from the empress.

sentences.zh: 至元二年崩，追謚詔慈皇后，升祔太宗廟。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhiyuan she died; posthumously honored as Empress Zhaoci and elevated to accompany Taizong in the temple.
translations.idiomatic: She died in 1265, was posthumously titled Empress Zhaoci, and was enshrined to accompany Taizong.

sentences.zh: 定宗欽淑皇后，名斡兀立海迷失。

translations.literal: Dingzong's Empress Qinshu, named Oghul Qaimish.
translations.idiomatic: Dingzong's Empress Qinshu was named Oghul Qaimish.

sentences.zh: 定宗崩，后抱子失列門垂簾聽政者六月。

translations.literal: When Dingzong died, the empress held her son Shiremün and governed behind the curtain for six months.
translations.idiomatic: When Güyük died, the empress held her son Shiremün and ruled from behind the curtain for six months.

sentences.zh: 至元二年，追謚欽淑皇后。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhiyuan, posthumously honored as Empress Qinshu.
translations.idiomatic: In 1265 she was posthumously titled Empress Qinshu.

sentences.zh: 憲宗貞節皇后，名忽都臺，弘吉剌氏，特薛禪孫忙哥陳之女也，蚤崩，后妹也速兒繼為妃。

translations.literal: Xianzong's Empress Zhenjie, named Qututai, of the Kongirat clan, was daughter of Möngke Chen, grandson of Tögüechü; she died early, and her younger sister Yesui succeeded as consort.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong's Empress Zhenjie, named Qututai, was of the Kongirat clan, daughter of Möngke Chen the grandson of Tögüechü; she died young, and her younger sister Yesui became consort in her stead.

sentences.zh: 至元二年，追謚貞節皇后，升祔憲宗廟。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhiyuan, posthumously honored as Empress Zhenjie and elevated to accompany Xianzong in the temple.
translations.idiomatic: In 1265 she was posthumously titled Empress Zhenjie and enshrined to accompany Möngke.

sentences.zh: 世祖昭睿順聖皇后，名察必，弘吉剌氏，濟寧忠武王按陳之女也。

translations.literal: Shizu's Empress Zhaorui Shunsheng, named Chabi, of the Kongirat clan, was daughter of the loyal and martial King Anchannayan of Jining.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu's Empress Zhaorui Shunsheng, named Chabi, was of the Kongirat clan and daughter of Anchannayan, loyal and martial King of Jining.

sentences.zh: 生裕宗。

translations.literal: She bore Yuzong.
translations.idiomatic: She bore Crown Prince Zhenjin.

sentences.zh: 中統初，立為皇后。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhongtong she was established as empress.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Zhongtong era she was made empress.

sentences.zh: 至元十年三月，授冊寶，上尊號貞懿昭聖順天睿文光應皇后。

translations.literal: In the third month of the tenth year of Zhiyuan she was invested with patent and seal, with honorific title Empress Zhenyi Zhaosheng Shuntian Ruiwen Guangying.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of 1273 she received patent and regalia, with the honorific title Empress Zhenyi Zhaosheng Shuntian Ruiwen Guangying.

sentences.zh: 一日，四怯薛官奏割京城外近地牧馬，帝既允，方以圖進。

translations.literal: One day an official of the four kheshig reported cutting nearby land outside the capital for pasturage; the emperor had already assented and the map was just being presented.
translations.idiomatic: One day a commander of the four kheshig proposed grazing horses on land just outside the capital; the emperor had already agreed and a map was being brought forward.

sentences.zh: 后至帝前，將諫，先陽責太保劉秉忠曰：「汝漢人聰明者，言則帝聽，汝何為不諫？

translations.literal: The empress came before the emperor to remonstrate; first she openly rebuked Grand Preceptor Liu Bingzhong, saying: "You are the clever one among the Han—when you speak the emperor listens; why do you not remonstrate?
translations.idiomatic: The empress came to remonstrate with the emperor; first she openly reproached Grand Preceptor Liu Bingzhong: "You are counted among the cleverest of the Han—when you speak, the emperor listens—so why did you not advise against this?

sentences.zh: 向初到定都時，若以地牧馬則可，今軍蘸俱分業已定，奪之可乎？

translations.literal: When we first came to fix the capital, pasturing there would have been possible; now the military households have all been assigned their trades—can we seize their holdings?
translations.idiomatic: When we first fixed the capital, grazing there might have been acceptable; but now the military households have all been assigned their livelihoods—can we simply seize their land?

sentences.zh: 」帝默然，命寢其事。

translations.literal: " The emperor was silent and ordered the matter dropped.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor fell silent and ordered the matter abandoned.

sentences.zh: 后嘗於太府監支繒帛表裏各一，帝謂后曰：「此軍國所需，非私家物，后何可得支？

translations.literal: The empress once drew silk fabrics, inner and outer, one each from the Imperial Storehouse; the emperor said to her: "These are needed for army and state—not private goods; how can the empress draw them?
translations.idiomatic: The empress once drew one bolt each of inner and outer silk from the Imperial Storehouse; the emperor told her: "These supplies belong to army and state, not to a private household—how can you take them?

sentences.zh: 」后自是率宮人親執女工，拘諸舊弓弦練之，緝為綢，以為衣，其韌密比綾綺。

translations.literal: " From then on the empress led the palace women in person to women's work, gathering old bowstrings and boiling them, weaving them into silk for clothing—its toughness and density rivaled damask.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereafter she led the palace women in person at needlework, collecting old bowstrings, boiling and weaving them into cloth for garments tough and fine as damask.

sentences.zh: 宣徽院羊臑皮置不用，后取之，合縫為地毯。

translations.literal: She took sheep fat from the Xuanhui Court that had been set aside unused, joined and sewed it into carpets.
translations.idiomatic: She took discarded sheep fat from the Xuanhui Court, stitched it together, and made carpets.

sentences.zh: 其勤儉有節而無棄物，類如此。

translations.literal: Her diligence and thrift with restraint and without waste were of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: Her thrift, restraint, and refusal to waste anything were characteristic in this way.

sentences.zh: 十三年，平宋，幼主朝於上都。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, when Song was pacified, the young ruler came to court at Shangdu.
translations.idiomatic: In 1276, when the Song was pacified, the young Song ruler came to court at Shangdu.

sentences.zh: 大宴，眾皆歡甚，唯后不樂。

translations.literal: At the great banquet all were exceedingly joyful, only the empress was not pleased.
translations.idiomatic: At the great banquet everyone rejoiced exceedingly, but the empress alone was not pleased.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「我今平江南，自此不用兵甲，眾人皆喜，爾獨不樂，何耶？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I have now pacified Jiangnan; from this we need no more arms—everyone is glad, yet you alone are not glad; why?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "I have now pacified the south; henceforth we need no more weapons—everyone is glad, yet you alone are not—why?

sentences.zh: 」后跪奏曰：「妾聞自古無千歲之國，毋使吾子孫及此，則幸矣。

translations.literal: " The empress knelt and replied: "Your subject has heard that since antiquity there has been no state of a thousand years; only let not our sons and grandsons come to this, and it will be fortune enough.
translations.idiomatic: " The empress knelt and answered: "I have heard that since antiquity no state has lasted a thousand years; if only our sons and grandsons never come to such an end, that will be fortune enough.

sentences.zh: 」帝以宋府庫故物各聚置殿庭上，召后視之，后遍視即去。

translations.literal: " The emperor had the Song palace stores' old goods all gathered and set out in the palace hall and summoned the empress to view them; she looked through them all and left.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor had the Song palace treasures gathered in the hall and summoned the empress to view them; she looked through everything and departed.

sentences.zh: 帝遣宦者追問后，欲何所取。

translations.literal: The emperor sent a eunuch to pursue and ask the empress what she wished to take.
translations.idiomatic: He sent a eunuch after her to ask what she wished to take.

sentences.zh: 后曰：「宋人貯蓄以遺其子孫，子孫不能守，而歸於我，我何忍取一物耶！

translations.literal: The empress said: "The Song people stored these to leave to their sons and grandsons; their sons and grandsons could not keep them and they have come to us—how can I bear to take a single thing!
translations.idiomatic: The empress replied: "The Song stored these for their sons and grandsons; their heirs could not keep them, and they have come to us—how could I bear to take even one thing?

sentences.zh: 」時宋太后全氏至京，不習北方風土，后為奏令回江南。

translations.literal: " At that time the Song Empress Dowager Quan had come to the capital and was unused to northern ways; the empress memorialized to let her return to Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: " At that time Song Empress Dowager Quan had reached the capital and was unused to northern customs; the empress memorialized that she be allowed to return to the south.

sentences.zh: 帝不允，至三奏，帝乃答曰：「爾婦人無遠慮，若使之南還，或浮言一動，即廢其家，非所以愛之也。

translations.literal: The emperor did not consent; after three memorials the emperor at last answered: "You women lack far-sighted planning; if we send her south, perhaps a single floating rumor would at once ruin her house—that is not how to love her.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused; after three memorials he answered at last: "You women lack far-sighted counsel; if we sent her south, a single rumor might at once destroy her household—that is not how to show care.

sentences.zh: 茍能愛之，時加存恤，使之便安可也。

translations.literal: If you can love her, from time to time show concern and support and let her live at ease—that will do.
translations.idiomatic: If you truly care for her, visit her often with kindness and let her live in comfort—that is enough.

sentences.zh: 」后退，益厚待之。

translations.literal: " The empress withdrew and treated her all the more generously.
translations.idiomatic: " The empress withdrew and treated her still more generously.

sentences.zh: 胡帽舊無前檐，帝因射日色炫目，以語后，后即益前檐。

translations.literal: Mongol caps formerly had no front brim; the emperor, because the sun's glare dazzled him when shooting, mentioned it to the empress, and she added a front brim.
translations.idiomatic: Mongol caps formerly had no front brim; because the sun dazzled him when he shot, the emperor mentioned it to the empress, and she extended the front brim.

sentences.zh: 帝大喜，遂命為式。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and ordered it made the standard.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and ordered it made the standard form.

sentences.zh: 又制一衣，前有裳無衽，后長倍於前，亦無領袖，綴以兩襻，名曰比甲，以便弓馬，時皆仿之。

translations.literal: She also devised a garment with a skirt in front but no overlapping lapel, the back twice the length of the front, also without collar or sleeves, fastened with two loops, called a bijia, convenient for bow and horse—at the time all imitated it.
translations.idiomatic: She also designed a garment with a skirt panel in front but no overlapping lapel, the back twice as long as the front, without collar or sleeves, fastened with two loops—called a bijia—convenient for bow and horse; everyone soon copied it.

sentences.zh: 后性明敏，達於事機，國家初政，左右匡正，當時與有力焉。

translations.literal: The empress was intelligent and clear, adept at affairs; in the state's first government she corrected matters left and right and at the time was thought to have great force.
translations.idiomatic: Intelligent and politically astute, she corrected affairs left and right in the dynasty's formative government and was widely thought to have wielded real influence.

sentences.zh: 十八年二月崩。

translations.literal: In the second month of the eighteenth year she died.
translations.idiomatic: She died in the second month of 1281.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，成宗即位，五月，追謚昭睿順聖皇后，其冊文曰：「奉先思孝，臣子之至情；

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year Chengzong took the throne; in the fifth month posthumously honored as Empress Zhaorui Shunsheng; the patent reads: "Serving the former and thinking of filial piety is the utmost feeling of subjects;
translations.idiomatic: When Chengzong took the throne in 1294, she was posthumously titled Empress Zhaorui Shunsheng in the fifth month; the patent reads: "Serving the departed and cherishing filial devotion is the utmost duty of subjects;

sentences.zh: 節惠易名，古今之大典。

translations.literal: regulating favor and changing the name is the great canon of antiquity and the present.
translations.idiomatic: tempering grace and changing the name is the great canon of antiquity and the present.

sentences.zh: 惟殷娥有明德之號，而周任著《思齊》之稱。

translations.literal: Only Yin E had the title of bright virtue, and Zhou Ren wrote of "Si Qi."
translations.idiomatic: Only Yin E bore the title of bright virtue, and Zhou Ren composed the "Si Qi."

sentences.zh: 爰考舊章，式崇尊謚。

translations.literal: We therefore examine the old regulations and exalt the honorific posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: We therefore examine the ancient statutes and exalt the honorific posthumous title.

sentences.zh: 恭惟先皇后，厚德載物，正位承天。

translations.literal: Respectfully: the late empress, with thick virtue bearing all things, took the correct position to receive Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Respectfully: the late empress, whose thick virtue bore all things, took the correct position to receive Heaven.

sentences.zh: 隆內治於公宮，綱大倫於天下。

translations.literal: She elevated inner rule in the public palace and set the great relations under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: She elevated inner governance in the palace and set the great relations of the realm in order.

sentences.zh: 曩事龍潛之邸，及乘虎變之秋。

translations.literal: Formerly she served the prince's hidden residence, and when he mounted the tiger's transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago she served the prince in his hidden residence, and when he mounted the throne in the hour of transformation.

sentences.zh: 鄂渚班師，洞識事機之會；

translations.literal: When the army withdrew at Ezhu she saw through the turn of affairs;
translations.idiomatic: When the army withdrew at Ezhou she grasped the turn of affairs;

sentences.zh: 上都踐祚，居多輔佐之謀。

translations.literal: when the throne was taken at Shangdu she mostly held plans of assistance.
translations.idiomatic: when the throne was taken at Shangdu she largely held the plans of assistance.

sentences.zh: 先物之明，獨斷於衷；

translations.literal: Foreknowledge of things first, deciding alone in the heart;
translations.idiomatic: Foreknowledge of affairs, deciding alone in her heart;

sentences.zh: 進賢之志，允葉於上。

translations.literal: the will to advance worthies, fully harmonizing with the sovereign above.
translations.idiomatic: the will to advance the worthy, fully harmonizing with the sovereign above.

sentences.zh: 左右我聖祖，建帝王之極功；

translations.literal: She assisted our sacred ancestor in establishing the utmost merit of emperors and kings;
translations.idiomatic: She assisted our sacred ancestor in establishing the utmost merit of emperors and kings;

sentences.zh: 撫育我前人，嗣社稷之重托。

translations.literal: she nurtured our forebears and undertook the heavy trust of the altars.
translations.idiomatic: she nurtured our forebears and undertook the heavy trust of the altars.

sentences.zh: 臣下之勸勞灼見，生民之疾苦周知。

translations.literal: The toil of subjects below was clearly seen; the suffering of the people was known all around.
translations.idiomatic: The toil of subjects below was plainly seen; the suffering of the people was known throughout.

sentences.zh: 儷宸極二十年，垂慈範千萬世。

translations.literal: She matched the Son of Heaven for twenty years and handed down a kindly model for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: She matched the Son of Heaven for twenty years and handed down a maternal model for ten thousand generations.

sentences.zh: 惟全美聖而益聖，宜顯冊書而屢書。

translations.literal: Only complete in sagehood and ever more sage—fitting to display the patent and write it again and again.
translations.idiomatic: Wholly complete in sagehood and ever more sage—fitting that the patent be displayed and written again and again.

sentences.zh: 不勝惓藐懇懇之誠，敬展尊尊親親之義，以揚盛烈，以對耿光。

translations.literal: Unable to overcome earnest, earnest sincerity, we respectfully unfold the meaning of honoring the honored and cherishing kin—thereby to raise the great achievement and answer the bright glory.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to overcome our earnest sincerity, we respectfully unfold the rite of honoring the honored and cherishing kin, to raise up her great achievement and answer her bright glory.

sentences.zh: 謹遣某官某奉玉冊玉寶，上尊謚曰昭睿順聖皇后。

translations.literal: We respectfully send Official [name] to present the jade patent and jade seal, with honorific posthumous title Empress Zhaorui Shunsheng.
translations.idiomatic: We respectfully dispatch Official [name] to present the jade patent and jade seal, conferring the honorific posthumous title Empress Zhaorui Shunsheng.

sentences.zh: 欽惟淑靈在天，明鑒逮下。

translations.literal: Respectfully: may her virtuous spirit be in Heaven; bright mirror reaching below.
translations.idiomatic: May her virtuous spirit be in Heaven; may her bright mirror reach below.

sentences.zh: 增輝煒管，茂揚徽懿之音；

translations.literal: Increase the splendor of the pipes; abundantly raise the sound of fine virtue;
translations.idiomatic: May splendor increase in the pipes; may the sound of her fine virtue be abundantly raised;

sentences.zh: 合饗太宮，益衍壽昌之福。

translations.literal: join in offering in the Grand Temple and further extend the blessing of long life and prosperity.
translations.idiomatic: may she share offerings in the Grand Temple and further extend the blessing of long life and prosperity.

sentences.zh: 」升祔世祖廟。

translations.literal: " Elevated to accompany Shizu in the temple.
translations.idiomatic: " She was enshrined to accompany Kublai in the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 南必皇后，弘吉剌氏，納陳孫仙童之女也。

translations.literal: Empress Nanbi, of the Kongirat clan, was daughter of Xiantong, grandson of Nachen.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Nanbi, of the Kongirat clan, was daughter of Xiantong, grandson of Nachen.

sentences.zh: 至元二十年，納為皇后，繼守正宮。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Zhiyuan she was taken in as empress and continued to guard the principal palace.
translations.idiomatic: In 1283 she was taken in as empress and continued to hold the principal palace.

sentences.zh: 時世祖春秋高，頗預政，相臣常不得見帝，輒因后奏事焉。

translations.literal: At that time Shizu was advanced in years and often participated in government; chief ministers frequently could not see the emperor and would present affairs through the empress.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai was then advanced in years and often preoccupied with government; chief ministers who could not reach the emperor would report affairs through her.

sentences.zh: 有子一人，名鐵蔑赤。

translations.literal: She had one son, named Temüke.
translations.idiomatic: She had one son, named Temüke.

sentences.zh: 卜魯罕皇后，伯嶽吾氏，駙馬脫裏思之女。

translations.literal: Empress Bulughan, of the Bayaut clan, was daughter of the imperial son-in-law Tögris.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Bulughan, of the Bayaut clan, was daughter of the imperial son-in-law Tögris.

sentences.zh: 元貞初，立為皇后。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanzhen she was established as empress.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Yuanzhen era she was made empress.

sentences.zh: 大德三年十月，授冊寶。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the third year of Dade she was invested with patent and seal.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of 1299 she was invested with patent and seal.

sentences.zh: 成宗多疾，后居中用事，信任相臣哈剌哈孫，大德之政，人稱平允，皆后處決。

translations.literal: Chengzong was often ill; the empress held sway within and trusted the chief minister Qaraghos; the government of the Dade era was called even and fair—all decided by the empress.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzong was often ill; the empress held power within and trusted Chief Minister Qaraghos; the Dade-era government was called even and fair—decisions came from her.

sentences.zh: 京師創建萬寧寺，中塑秘密佛像，其形醜怪，后以手帕蒙覆其面，尋傳旨毀之。

translations.literal: In the capital the Wanning Temple was built, with secret Buddha images inside whose forms were ugly and strange; the empress covered their faces with a handkerchief and soon ordered them destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: When Wanning Temple was built in the capital, secret Buddha images were placed inside, ugly and grotesque in form; the empress covered their faces with a handkerchief and soon ordered them destroyed.

sentences.zh: 省院臺臣奏上尊號，帝不允。

translations.literal: The provincial, court, and censorial ministers memorialized an honorific title; the emperor did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers of the Secretariat, Court, and Censorate memorialized an honorific title; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 車駕幸上都，后方自奏請。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage went to Shangdu, the empress herself memorialized the request.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor traveled to Shangdu, the empress herself submitted the request.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「我病日久，國家大事多廢不舉，尚寧理此等事耶！

translations.literal: The emperor said: "My illness has been long; great affairs of state are mostly abandoned and not undertaken—how can I still manage such matters!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "My illness has been long; great affairs of state lie mostly abandoned—how can I still attend to such things?

sentences.zh: 」事遂寢。

translations.literal: " The matter was then dropped.
translations.idiomatic: " The matter was then dropped.

sentences.zh: 大德十年，后嘗謀貶順宗妃答吉與其子仁宗往懷州。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Dade the empress once plotted to demote Shunzong's consort Dagi and her son Renzong to Huai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In 1306 the empress once plotted to demote Shunzong's consort Dagi and her son Renzong to Huai Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 明年，成宗崩。

translations.literal: The next year Chengzong died.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Chengzong died.

sentences.zh: 時武宗在北邊，恐其歸，必報前怨，后乃命取安西王阿難答失裏來京師，謀立之。

translations.literal: At that time Wuzong was on the northern frontier; fearing his return and sure revenge for old grievances, the empress ordered Prince Anxi Ananda brought to the capital to plot enthroning him.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzong was then on the northern frontier; fearing his return and reprisal for old grievances, she ordered Prince Anxi Ananda brought to the capital, intending to set him on the throne.

sentences.zh: 仁宗自懷州入清宮禁，既誅安西王，並構后以私通事，出居東安州。

translations.literal: Renzong entered from Huai Prefecture and cleared the inner palace; after Anxi was executed, he also framed the empress on charges of illicit relations and removed her to Dong'an Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Renzong entered from Huai Prefecture, secured the inner palace, executed Prince Anxi, and also framed the empress on charges of illicit relations, sending her to live at Dong'an Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 武宗宣慈惠聖皇后，名真哥，弘吉剌氏，脫憐子迸不剌之女。

translations.literal: Wuzong's Empress Xuanhui Huisheng, named Zhenge, of the Kongirat clan, was daughter of Temülen's son Bintuqla.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzong's Empress Xuanhui Huisheng, named Zhenge, was of the Kongirat clan, daughter of Bintuqla son of Temülen.

sentences.zh: 至大三年四月，冊為皇后，其文曰：「乾為天，坤為地，四時由是以相成，日宗陽，月宗陰，萬象以之而並著。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the third year of Zhida she was enregistered as empress; the text reads: "Qian is Heaven, Kun is Earth; the four seasons thereby achieve mutual completion; the sun honors yang, the moon honors yin; the myriad images thereby appear together.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of 1310 she was enregistered as empress; the patent reads: "Qian is Heaven and Kun is Earth; through them the four seasons achieve their mutual completion; the sun honors yang and the moon honors yin; through them the myriad phenomena stand forth together.

sentences.zh: 后職有關於世教，先猷具載於邦彜。

translations.literal: The office of empress concerns the teachings of the age; the former models are fully recorded in state ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The office of empress bears on the moral instruction of the age; the models of former ages are fully set down in state ritual.

sentences.zh: 惟慈旨之親承，亦僉言之允若。

translations.literal: Only the kindly purpose personally received, and the unanimous words approving.
translations.idiomatic: She has personally received the court's kindly intent, and unanimous approval has followed.

sentences.zh: 咨爾皇后弘吉剌氏，睿聰淑哲，端懿誠莊。

translations.literal: We address you, Empress of the Kongirat clan: perspicacious, intelligent, pure and wise, upright, excellent, sincere, and dignified.
translations.idiomatic: We address you, Empress of the Kongirat clan—perspicacious and wise, upright, sincere, and dignified.

sentences.zh: 寶婺分輝，源天潢之自出；

translations.literal: The constellation Maiden divides its radiance; her source springs from the Heavenly Clan itself;
translations.idiomatic: Like the Maiden constellation she shares in heaven's radiance, sprung from the imperial clan itself;

sentences.zh: 纓徽迪慶，系紱組以相仍。

translations.literal: tassels and insignia extend blessings; the cord and seal pass on in succession.
translations.idiomatic: her tassels and insignia extend blessings, and cord and seal pass down in unbroken succession.

translations.literal: 〈 lacuna opens
translations.idiomatic: The text here is missing from the manuscript.

sentences.zh: （後逸）〉

translations.literal: (text lost) 〉 [lacuna closes]
translations.idiomatic: (The remainder of the investiture text is lost.) 〉

sentences.zh: 」皇慶二年，立長秋寺，掌皇后宮政，秩三品。

translations.literal: " In the second year of Huangqing the Changqiu Office was established to manage the empress's palace government, rank third grade.
translations.idiomatic: " In 1313 the Changqiu Office was established to administer the empress's palace affairs, at the third rank.

sentences.zh: 泰定四年十一月崩，上尊謚曰宣慈惠聖皇后，升祔武宗廟。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the fourth year of Taiding she died; honored with posthumous title Empress Xuanhui Huisheng and elevated to accompany Wuzong in the temple.
translations.idiomatic: She died in the eleventh month of 1327, was posthumously titled Empress Xuanhui Huisheng, and was enshrined to accompany Wuzong.

sentences.zh: 速哥失裏皇后，按陳哈兒只之女、真哥皇后之從妹也。

translations.literal: Empress Sugabali, daughter of Anchü Qariji, was a younger cousin of Empress Zhenge.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Sugabali, daughter of Anchü Qariji, was a younger cousin of Empress Zhenge.

sentences.zh: 妃二人：亦乞烈氏，奴兀倫公主之女，實生明宗，天歷二年追謚仁獻章聖皇后；

translations.literal: Two consorts: one of the Ikiret clan, daughter of Princess Nuwulun, who actually bore Mingzong—in the second year of Tianli posthumously titled Empress Renxian Zhangsheng;
translations.idiomatic: Two consorts: one of the Ikiret clan, daughter of Princess Nuwulun, who actually bore Mingzong—in 1329 posthumously titled Empress Renxian Zhangsheng;

sentences.zh: 唐兀氏，生文宗，天歷二年追謚文獻昭聖皇后。

translations.literal: one of the Tangut clan, who bore Wenzong—in the second year of Tianli posthumously titled Empress Wenxian Zhaosheng.
translations.idiomatic: one of the Tangut clan, who bore Wenzong—in 1329 posthumously titled Empress Wenxian Zhaosheng.

sentences.zh: 仁宗莊懿慈聖皇后，名阿納失失裏，弘吉剌氏，生英宗。

translations.literal: Renzong's Empress Zhuangyi Cisheng, named Anaushir, of the Kongirat clan, bore Yingzong.
translations.idiomatic: Renzong's Empress Zhuangyi Cisheng, named Anaushir, was of the Kongirat clan and bore Yingzong.

sentences.zh: 皇慶二年三月，冊為皇后，上冊寶，遣官祭告天地於南郊及太廟。

translations.literal: In the third month of the second year of Huangqing she was enregistered as empress, with patent and seal invested; officials were dispatched to report to Heaven and Earth at the southern suburb and at the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of 1313 she was enregistered as empress with patent and seal, and officials were sent to report to Heaven and Earth at the southern suburb and at the Grand Temple.

sentences.zh: 改典內院為中政院，秩正二品。

translations.literal: The Inner Court was changed to the Central Administration, rank upper second grade.
translations.idiomatic: The Inner Court was reorganized as the Central Administration, at the upper second rank.

sentences.zh: 英宗即位，上尊號皇太后，其冊文曰：「坤承乾德，所以著兩儀之稱；

translations.literal: When Yingzong took the throne, she was honored as Empress Dowager; the patent reads: "Kun receives Qian's virtue, thereby displaying the title of the two principles;
translations.idiomatic: When Yingzong took the throne, she was honored as Empress Dowager; the patent reads: "Kun receives Qian's virtue, thereby displaying the title of the two principles;

sentences.zh: 母統父尊，所以崇一體之號。

translations.literal: the mother sets the father's honor, thereby exalting the title of the single body.
translations.idiomatic: the mother sets the father's honor, thereby exalting the title of the single body.

sentences.zh: 故因親而立愛，宜考禮以正名。

translations.literal: Therefore through kinship one establishes love; one should examine ritual to correct the name.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore through kinship one establishes love; ritual should be examined to correct the name.

sentences.zh: 恭惟聖母，溫慈惠和，淑哲端懿。

translations.literal: Respectfully: the Sacred Mother, warm, kindly, gracious, and harmonious, pure, wise, upright, and excellent.
translations.idiomatic: Respectfully: the Sacred Mother—warm, kindly, gracious, and harmonious; pure, wise, upright, and excellent.

sentences.zh: 上以奉宗祧之重，下以敘倫紀之常。

translations.literal: Above she served the weight of the ancestral temple; below she ordered the constant of human relations.
translations.idiomatic: Above she served the weight of the ancestral temple; below she ordered the constant of human relations.

sentences.zh: 恢王化於二南，嗣徽音於三母。

translations.literal: She restored royal transformation in the "Two Souths" and continued fine reputation among the Three Mothers.
translations.idiomatic: She restored royal transformation in the Two Souths and continued fine reputation among the Three Mothers.

sentences.zh: 輔佐先考，憂勤警戒之慮深；

translations.literal: She assisted the late emperor with deep concern for diligence and vigilance;
translations.idiomatic: She assisted the late emperor with deep concern for diligence and vigilance;

sentences.zh: 擁佑眇躬，撫育提攜之恩至。

translations.literal: she embraced and protected our young person with utmost grace in nurture and guidance.
translations.idiomatic: she embraced and protected our young person with utmost grace in nurture and guidance.

sentences.zh: 迨於今日，紹我丕基。

translations.literal: Down to this day she continues our great foundation.
translations.idiomatic: Down to this day she continues our great foundation.

sentences.zh: 規摹一出於慈闈，付托益彰於祖訓。

translations.literal: Plans and models all issued from the kindly quarter; entrustment further displayed the ancestral instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Plans and models all issued from the kindly quarter; entrustment further displayed the ancestral instruction.

sentences.zh: 致天下之養以為樂，未足盡於孝心；

translations.literal: To bring the nourishment of all under Heaven as joy is not enough to exhaust filial heart;
translations.idiomatic: To bring the nourishment of all under Heaven as joy is not enough to exhaust filial heart;

sentences.zh: 極域中之大以為尊，庶可稱其懿美。

translations.literal: to extend the greatest within the realm as honor may fittingly praise her excellent beauty.
translations.idiomatic: to extend the greatest honor within the realm may fittingly praise her excellent virtue.

sentences.zh: 式遵貴貴之義，用罄親親之情。

translations.literal: We follow the meaning of honoring the honored and exhaust the feeling of cherishing kin.
translations.idiomatic: We follow the meaning of honoring the honored and exhaust the feeling of cherishing kin.

sentences.zh: 謹遣某官某奉冊，上尊號曰皇太后。

translations.literal: We respectfully send Official [name] to present the patent, with honorific title Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: We respectfully dispatch Official [name] to present the patent, conferring the honorific title Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 伏惟周宗綿綿，長信穆穆，備《洛書》之錫福，粲坤極之儀天。

translations.literal: We humbly hope the Zhou clan endures in abundance, Changxin is solemn and reverent, fully receiving the blessing bestowed in the "Luoshu," brilliantly manifesting the rites of the utmost yin matching Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: May the Zhou clan endure in abundance and Changxin stand solemn and reverent, fully receiving the blessing of the Luoshu and brilliantly manifesting the rites of the utmost yin matching Heaven.

sentences.zh: 啟佑后人，永錫胤祚。

translations.literal: Open protection for posterity; forever bestow succession.
translations.idiomatic: Open protection for posterity; forever bestow succession.

sentences.zh: 」明日，受百官朝賀於興聖宮。

translations.literal: " The next day she received the hundred officials' homage at Xingsheng Palace.
translations.idiomatic: " The next day she received the homage of the hundred officials at Xingsheng Palace.

sentences.zh: 至治二年崩，上謚莊懿慈聖皇后，其冊文曰：「致孝所以揚親，易名所以表行。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhizhi she died; honored with posthumous title Empress Zhuangyi Cisheng; the patent reads: "To fulfill filial piety is to raise up kin; to change the name is to display conduct.
translations.idiomatic: She died in 1322 and was posthumously titled Empress Zhuangyi Cisheng; the patent reads: "To fulfill filial piety is to raise up kin; to change the name is to display conduct.

sentences.zh: 矧為天下母而養弗逮，履天子位而報則豐。

translations.literal: How much more for the mother of all under Heaven when nourishment did not reach her, yet treading the Son of Heaven's position the return is abundant.
translations.idiomatic: How much more for the mother of all under Heaven, when nourishment did not reach her in life, yet on the Son of Heaven's throne the return is abundant.

sentences.zh: 曷勝孺慕之心，必盡欽崇之禮。

translations.literal: Unable to overcome childlike longing, one must fully perform the reverent honoring rites.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to overcome childlike longing, one must fully perform the reverent honoring rites.

sentences.zh: 欽惟先皇太后，夙明壸則，克嗣徽音。

translations.literal: Respectfully: the late Empress Dowager, from of old clear in the rules of the inner quarter, fully continued fine reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Respectfully: the late Empress Dowager, from of old clear in the rules of the inner quarter, fully continued fine reputation.

sentences.zh: 輔佐先朝，有恭儉節用之實；

translations.literal: She assisted the former court with the reality of respectful thrift and regulated use;
translations.idiomatic: She assisted the former court with the reality of respectful thrift and regulated use;

sentences.zh: 誕育眇質，有劬勞顧復之恩。

translations.literal: she bore our young substance with the grace of laborious nurture and restoration.
translations.idiomatic: she bore our young person with the grace of laborious nurture and restoration.

sentences.zh: 九族咸育於仁，四海仰遵其化。

translations.literal: The nine kindreds were all nurtured in benevolence; the four seas looked up and followed her transformation.
translations.idiomatic: The nine kindreds were all nurtured in benevolence; the four seas looked up and followed her transformation.

sentences.zh: 昊天不吊，景命靡融。

translations.literal: High Heaven did not pity; the bright mandate did not harmonize.
translations.idiomatic: High Heaven did not pity; the bright mandate did not harmonize.

sentences.zh: 愴聖善之長違，念風猷之未泯。

translations.literal: Grieved that the sacred goodness was long departed, we think of her wind and teaching not yet extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Grieved that sacred goodness was long departed, we recall her wind and teaching not yet extinguished.

sentences.zh: 是用揄揚於彤史，正宜敷繹於寶慈。

translations.literal: Therefore we praise her in the vermilion histories; it is fitting to unfold her in treasured kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore we praise her in the vermilion histories; it is fitting to unfold her in treasured kindness.

sentences.zh: 爰據彜經，追嚴徽號。

translations.literal: We therefore follow the constant canon and pursue a strict honorific title.
translations.idiomatic: We therefore follow the constant canon and pursue a strict honorific title.

sentences.zh: 謹遣攝太慰某官某奉玉冊玉寶，上尊號曰莊懿慈聖皇后。

translations.literal: We respectfully send the Acting Grand Marshal Official [name] to present the jade patent and jade seal, with honorific posthumous title Empress Zhuangyi Cisheng.
translations.idiomatic: We respectfully dispatch the Acting Grand Marshal Official [name] to present the jade patent and jade seal, conferring the honorific posthumous title Empress Zhuangyi Cisheng.

sentences.zh: 伏惟淑靈如在，合饗太宮。

translations.literal: We humbly hope her virtuous spirit is as if present; join in offering in the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: May her virtuous spirit be as if present; may she join in offering in the Grand Temple.

sentences.zh: 鑒格孔昭，膺茲巨典。

translations.literal: Inspection and reception are greatly manifest; receive this great canon.
translations.idiomatic: May inspection and reception be greatly manifest; may she receive this great canon.

sentences.zh: 陰相丕祚，億萬斯年。

translations.literal: Yin assists the great fortune; ten thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: May yin assist the great fortune for ten thousand years.

sentences.zh: 」升祔仁宗廟。

translations.literal: " Elevated to accompany Renzong in the temple.
translations.idiomatic: " She was enshrined to accompany Renzong in the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 英宗莊靜懿聖皇后，名速哥八剌，亦啟烈氏，昌國公主益裏海涯女也。

translations.literal: Yingzong's Empress Zhuangjing Yisheng, named Sugabala, also of the Ikiret clan, was daughter of Princess Yilihaiya of Changguo.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzong's Empress Zhuangjing Yisheng, named Sugabala, also of the Ikiret clan, was daughter of Princess Yilihaiya of Changguo.

sentences.zh: 至治元年，冊為皇后。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhizhi she was enregistered as empress.
translations.idiomatic: In 1321 she was enregistered as empress.

sentences.zh: 泰定四年六月崩，謚曰莊靜懿聖皇后。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fourth year of Taiding she died; posthumously titled Empress Zhuangjing Yisheng.
translations.idiomatic: She died in the sixth month of 1327 and was posthumously titled Empress Zhuangjing Yisheng.

sentences.zh: 妃二人：一曰必罕，一曰速哥答裏，皆弘吉剌氏，兗王買住罕之女也。

translations.literal: Two consorts: one named Bihan, one named Sugabali—both of the Kongirat clan, daughters of Prince Yan Buyanhan.
translations.idiomatic: Two consorts: one named Bihan, one named Sugabali—both of the Kongirat clan, daughters of Prince Yan Buyanhan.

sentences.zh: 文宗天歷初，俱安置東安州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wenzong's Tianli reign both were settled at Dong'an Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Wenzong's Tianli reign both were settled at Dong'an Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 明宗貞裕徽聖皇后，名邁來迪，生順帝而崩。

translations.literal: Mingzong's Empress Zhenyu Huisheng, named Mailaiti, bore Shundi and died.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong's Empress Zhenyu Huisheng, named Mailaiti, bore Shundi and died.

sentences.zh: 文宗立，謚貞裕徽聖皇后。

translations.literal: When Wenzong took the throne, posthumously titled Empress Zhenyu Huisheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenzong took the throne, she was posthumously titled Empress Zhenyu Huisheng.

sentences.zh: 八不沙皇后，成宗甥壽寧公主之女也。

translations.literal: Empress Babusha was daughter of Chengzong's niece, Princess Shouning.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Babusha was daughter of Chengzong's niece, Princess Shouning.

sentences.zh: 侍明宗潛邸，生寧宗。

translations.literal: She attended Mingzong in his hidden residence and bore Ningzong.
translations.idiomatic: She attended Mingzong in his hidden residence and bore Ningzong.

sentences.zh: 天歷二年，立寧徽寺，掌明宗皇后宮事，以鈔萬錠、幣帛二千匹，供後宮費用。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianli the Ninghui Office was established to manage Mingzong's empress's palace affairs, with ten thousand ingots of paper money and two thousand bolts of silk and cloth for the inner palace's expenses.
translations.idiomatic: In 1329 the Ninghui Office was established to manage Mingzong's empress's palace affairs, with ten thousand ingots of paper money and two thousand bolts of silk and cloth for inner-palace expenses.

sentences.zh: 十一月，后請為明宗資冥福，命帝師率諸僧作佛事七日於大天源延聖寺，道士建醮於玉虛、天寶、太乙、萬壽四宮，及武當、龍虎二山。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month the empress requested merit for Mingzong's departed spirit; the emperor ordered the Imperial Preceptor to lead the monks in Buddhist rites for seven days at the Great Tianyuan Yansheng Temple, and Daoists to perform offerings at the four palaces Yuxu, Tianbao, Taiyi, and Wanshou, and at the two mountains Wudang and Longhu.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the empress requested merit for Mingzong's departed spirit; the emperor ordered the Imperial Preceptor to lead monks in seven days of Buddhist rites at the Great Tianyuan Yansheng Temple, and Daoists to perform offerings at the Yuxu, Tianbao, Taiyi, and Wanshou palaces and at Wudang and Longhu mountains.

sentences.zh: 至順元年，敕有司供明宗後宮幣帛二百匹。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhishun an edict ordered the relevant offices to supply two hundred bolts of silk and cloth for Mingzong's inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: In 1330 an edict ordered the relevant offices to supply two hundred bolts of silk and cloth for Mingzong's inner palace.

sentences.zh: 是年四月崩。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of that year she died.
translations.idiomatic: She died in the fourth month of that year.

sentences.zh: 文宗卜答失裏皇后，弘吉剌氏，父駙馬魯王雕阿不剌，母魯國公主桑哥剌吉。

translations.literal: Wenzong's Empress Budashiri, of the Kongirat clan—her father was the imperial son-in-law Prince Lu Diaobula; her mother was Princess Lu of the Lu state, Sanggaraji.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzong's Empress Budashiri was of the Kongirat clan; her father was the imperial son-in-law Prince Lu Diaobula, and her mother was Princess Lu Sanggaraji.

sentences.zh: 文宗居建業，后亦在行。

translations.literal: When Wenzong resided at Jianye, the empress was also on the journey.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenzong resided at Jianye, the empress accompanied him.

sentences.zh: 天歷元年，文宗即位，立為皇后。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianli Wenzong took the throne and she was established as empress.
translations.idiomatic: In 1328 Wenzong took the throne and she was made empress.

sentences.zh: 二年，授冊寶。

translations.literal: In the second year she was invested with patent and seal.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year she received patent and seal.

sentences.zh: 十一月，后以銀五萬兩助建大承天護聖寺。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month the empress contributed fifty thousand taels of silver to help build the Great Chengtian Husheng Temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the empress contributed fifty thousand taels of silver toward building the Great Chengtian Husheng Temple.

sentences.zh: 至順元年，以籍沒張珪家田四百頃，賜護聖寺為永業。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhishun four hundred qing of fields from the confiscated estate of Zhang Gui were bestowed on Husheng Temple as perpetual property.
translations.idiomatic: In 1330 four hundred qing of fields from Zhang Gui's confiscated estate were granted to Husheng Temple as perpetual property.

sentences.zh: 后與宦者拜住謀殺明宗后八不沙。

translations.literal: The empress and the eunuch Baiyu plotted to kill Mingzong's empress Babusha.
translations.idiomatic: The empress and the eunuch Baiyu plotted to kill Mingzong's empress Babusha.

sentences.zh: 三年八月，文宗崩於上都，后導揚末命，申帝初誌，遂立明宗次子懿璘質班，是為寧宗。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the third year Wenzong died at Shangdu; the empress guided his final command and declared the emperor's original intent, then established Mingzong's second son Rinchinbal—this is Ningzong.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of 1332 Wenzong died at Shangdu; the empress guided his final command and declared the emperor's original intent, establishing Mingzong's second son Rinchinbal as Ningzong.

sentences.zh: 十一月，奉玉冊玉寶尊皇后為皇太后。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month jade patent and jade seal were presented to honor the empress as Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month jade patent and seal were presented to honor her as Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 十二月，禦興聖殿受朝賀。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month she held court at Xingsheng Hall to receive homage.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month she held court at Xingsheng Hall to receive homage.

sentences.zh: 寧宗崩，大臣請立太子燕貼古思。

translations.literal: When Ningzong died, the great ministers requested enthroning the crown prince Yantigush.
translations.idiomatic: When Ningzong died, the great ministers requested enthroning the crown prince Yantigush.

sentences.zh: 后曰：「天位至重，吾子尚幼，明宗長子妥歡帖睦爾在廣西，今十三歲矣，理當立之。

translations.literal: The empress said: "The heavenly throne is of utmost weight; my son is still young; Mingzong's eldest son Toghontemür is in Guangxi, now thirteen years of age—he ought rightly to be established.
translations.idiomatic: The empress said: "The throne is of utmost weight; my son is still young; Mingzong's eldest son Toghontemür is in Guangxi, now thirteen—he ought to be established.

sentences.zh: 」於是奉旨迎至京師，以明年六月即位，是為順帝。

translations.literal: " Thereupon they received the edict to welcome him to the capital; in the sixth month of the next year he took the throne—this is Shundi.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict welcomed him to the capital; in the sixth month of the following year he took the throne as Shundi.

sentences.zh: 元統元年，尊為太皇太后，仍稱制臨朝。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuantong she was honored as Grand Empress Dowager and still governed as regent.
translations.idiomatic: In 1333 she was honored as Grand Empress Dowager and still governed as regent.

sentences.zh: 至元六年六月，詔去尊號，安置東安州，尋崩。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the sixth year of Zhiyuan an edict removed her honorific title; she was settled at Dong'an Prefecture and soon died.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of 1340 an edict removed her honorific title; she was settled at Dong'an Prefecture and soon died.

sentences.zh: 寧宗答裏也忒迷失皇后，弘吉剌氏。

translations.literal: Ningzong's Empress Danayetmishi, of the Kongirat clan.
translations.idiomatic: Ningzong's Empress Danayetmishi, of the Kongirat clan.

sentences.zh: 至順三年十月，立為后。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the third year of Zhishun she was established as empress.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of 1332 she was made empress.

sentences.zh: 至正二十八年崩，升祔寧宗廟。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year of Zhizheng she died and was elevated to accompany Ningzong in the temple.
translations.idiomatic: She died in 1368 and was enshrined to accompany Ningzong.

sentences.zh: 順帝答納失裏皇后，欽察氏，太師平王燕鐵木兒之女。

translations.literal: Shundi's Empress Danashirin, of the Qipchaq clan, daughter of Grand Preceptor and Prince Ping El Temür.
translations.idiomatic: Shundi's Empress Danashirin, of the Qipchaq clan, was daughter of Grand Preceptor and Prince Ping El Temür.

sentences.zh: 至順四年，立為后。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhishun she was established as empress.
translations.idiomatic: In 1333 she was made empress.

sentences.zh: 元統二年，授冊寶，其冊文曰：「天之元統二氣，配莫厚於坤儀；

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuantong she was invested with patent and seal; the patent reads: "Heaven's primal unity of the two qi—none thicker in pairing than the kun ritual;
translations.idiomatic: In 1334 she received patent and seal; the patent reads: "Heaven's primal unity of the two qi—none thicker in pairing than the kun ritual;

sentences.zh: 月之道循右行，明周貞於乾曜。

translations.literal: the moon's way follows the rightward course; brightness completes constancy in the qian radiance.
translations.idiomatic: the moon's way follows the rightward course; brightness completes constancy in the qian radiance.

sentences.zh: 若昔帝王之宅後，居多輔相之世勛。

translations.literal: Formerly when emperors and kings dwelt in the rear, they mostly relied on assisting ministers of generations of merit.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly when emperors and kings chose consorts, they mostly relied on assisting ministers of generations of merit.

sentences.zh: 蓋選德於亢宗，亦疇庸於先正。

translations.literal: They selected virtue from the lofty clan and also apportioned merit to the former upright.
translations.idiomatic: They selected virtue from the lofty clan and also apportioned merit to former upright ministers.

sentences.zh: 造周資任、姒之化，興漢表馬、鄧之功。

translations.literal: Zhou was aided by the transformation of Ren and Si; Han displayed the merit of Ma and Deng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou was aided by the transformation of Ren and Si; Han displayed the merit of Ma and Deng.

sentences.zh: 咨爾皇后欽察氏，雍肅惠慈，謙裕靜淑。

translations.literal: We address you, Empress of the Qipchaq clan: dignified, solemn, gracious, kindly, modest, abundant, quiet, and pure.
translations.idiomatic: We address you, Empress of the Qipchaq clan—dignified, solemn, gracious, kindly, modest, abundant, quiet, and pure.

sentences.zh: 乃祖乃父，夙堅翼亮之心；

translations.literal: Your grandfathers and fathers from of old firmly held the heart of winged assistance;
translations.idiomatic: Your grandfathers and fathers from of old firmly held the heart of loyal assistance;

sentences.zh: 於國於家，實獲修齊之助。

translations.literal: for state and family they truly obtained the help of cultivation and ordering.
translations.idiomatic: for state and family they truly obtained the help of cultivation and ordering.

sentences.zh: 朕纘丕圖之初載，親承太后之睿謨。

translations.literal: We continue the first undertaking of the great plan and personally receive the Empress Dowager's perspicacious strategy.
translations.idiomatic: We continue the first undertaking of the great plan and personally receive the Empress Dowager's perspicacious strategy.

sentences.zh: 眷我元臣，簡茲碩媛。

translations.literal: We cherish our Yuan minister and select this great lady.
translations.idiomatic: We cherish our Yuan minister and select this great lady.

sentences.zh: 相嚴禘而率典，奉慈極以愉顏。

translations.literal: Together we perform the solemn sacrifices and lead the canon; we serve the kindly pole with a pleased countenance.
translations.idiomatic: Together we perform the solemn sacrifices and lead the canon; we serve the kindly pole with a pleased countenance.

sentences.zh: 用彰祎翟之華，式著旗常之舊。

translations.literal: We thereby display the splendor of the pheasant robes and manifest the old standards of banner and constant.
translations.idiomatic: We thereby display the splendor of the pheasant robes and manifest the old standards of banner and constant.

sentences.zh: 令攝太尉某官授以玉冊寶章，命爾為皇后。

translations.literal: We order the Acting Grand Marshal Official to confer the jade patent and treasure seal and command you as empress.
translations.idiomatic: We order the Acting Grand Marshal Official to confer the jade patent and treasure seal and command you as empress.

sentences.zh: 備成嘉禮，宏賁太猷。

translations.literal: Complete the accomplished rites and grandly display the great plan.
translations.idiomatic: Complete the accomplished rites and grandly display the great plan.

sentences.zh: 於戲！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 嵩高生賢，予篤懷於良佐；

translations.literal: Songgao produces the worthy; we deeply cherish the good assistant;
translations.idiomatic: Songgao produces the worthy; we deeply cherish the good assistant;

sentences.zh: 《關雎》正始，爾勉嗣於徽音。

translations.literal: "Guanju" is the correct beginning—you must strive to continue fine reputation.
translations.idiomatic: "Guanju" is the correct beginning—you must strive to continue fine reputation.

sentences.zh: 永錫壽康，昭示悠久。

translations.literal: Forever bestow long life and health; broadly display enduringness.
translations.idiomatic: Forever bestow long life and health; broadly display enduringness.

sentences.zh: 」三年，后兄御史大夫唐其勢以謀逆誅，弟塔剌海走匿后宮，后以衣蔽之，因遷后出宮，丞相伯顏鴆后於開平民舍。

translations.literal: " In the third year the empress's elder brother, Censor-in-Chief Tangkiši, was executed for plotting rebellion; her younger brother Talahai fled and hid in the inner palace; the empress covered him with her robe; therefore she was removed from the palace, and Chief Minister Bayan poisoned the empress at a lodge in Kaiping.
translations.idiomatic: " In the third year the empress's elder brother, Censor-in-Chief Tangkiši, was executed for plotting rebellion; her younger brother Talahai fled into the inner palace and the empress hid him with her robe; she was therefore removed from the palace, and Chief Minister Bayan poisoned her at a lodge in Kaiping.

sentences.zh: 伯顏忽都皇后，弘吉剌氏，宣慈惠聖皇后真哥侄毓德王孛羅帖木兒之女也。

translations.literal: Empress Bayan Qudu, of the Kongirat clan, was daughter of Prince Yude Boluotiemür, nephew of Empress Xuanhui Huisheng Zhenge.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Bayan Qudu, of the Kongirat clan, was daughter of Prince Yude Boluotiemür, nephew of Empress Xuanhui Huisheng Zhenge.

sentences.zh: 至元三年三月，立為皇后。

translations.literal: In the third month of the third year of Zhiyuan she was established as empress.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of 1335 she was made empress.

sentences.zh: 其冊文曰：「帝王之道，齊其家而天下平；

translations.literal: The patent reads: "The way of emperors and kings is to order the family and all under Heaven is pacified;
translations.idiomatic: The patent reads: "The way of emperors and kings is to order the family and thereby pacify all under Heaven;

sentences.zh: 風教所基，正乎位而人倫厚。

translations.literal: what custom and teaching take as foundation is correcting the position, and human relations are thereby made thick.
translations.idiomatic: what custom and teaching rest upon is the correct position, through which human relations are deepened.

sentences.zh: 爰擇配以承宗事，若稽古以率典常。

translations.literal: We therefore select a mate to undertake the ancestral sacrifices and examine antiquity to lead the constant canon.
translations.idiomatic: We therefore choose a consort to undertake the ancestral sacrifices and examine antiquity to uphold the constant canon.

sentences.zh: 咨爾弘吉剌氏，淑哲溫恭，齊莊貞一。

translations.literal: We address you of the Kongirat clan: pure, wise, warm, and respectful, even, dignified, upright, and single-minded.
translations.idiomatic: We address you of the Kongirat clan—pure, wise, warm, respectful, even, dignified, upright, and single-minded.

sentences.zh: 屬選賢於中壸，躬受命於慈闈。

translations.literal: Belonging to the selection of worthies in the inner quarter, you personally received command in the kindly quarter.
translations.idiomatic: Chosen as a worthy in the inner quarter, you personally received command from the Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 勖帥來嬪，蹈榘儀之有度；

translations.literal: You exhorted and led the coming bride, treading the compass of ritual with measure;
translations.idiomatic: You exhorted and led the coming bride, treading the compass of ritual with proper measure;

sentences.zh: 動容中禮，謹夙夜以無違。

translations.literal: in bearing and countenance you conformed to ritual, diligently keeping day and night without violation.
translations.idiomatic: in bearing and countenance you conformed to ritual, diligently keeping day and night without violation.

sentences.zh: 茲表式於宮庭，宜推崇其位號。

translations.literal: Now display the model in the palace court; it is fitting to exalt your position and title.
translations.idiomatic: Now you display the model in the palace court; it is fitting to exalt your position and title.

sentences.zh: 乃蠲吉旦，庸舉彜章，遣攝太尉某持節授以玉冊寶章，命爾為皇后。

translations.literal: We therefore choose an auspicious day and broadly perform the constant canon, sending the Acting Grand Marshal [name] bearing credentials to confer the jade patent and treasure seal and command you as empress.
translations.idiomatic: We therefore choose an auspicious day and perform the constant canon, dispatching the Acting Grand Marshal [name] bearing credentials to confer the jade patent and treasure seal and command you as empress.

sentences.zh: 於戲！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 乾施坤承，克順成於四序；

translations.literal: Qian bestows and Kun receives; fully compliant, it is achieved in the four seasons;
translations.idiomatic: Qian bestows and Kun receives; fully compliant, harmony is achieved through the four seasons;

sentences.zh: 日明月儷，久照臨於萬方。

translations.literal: sun bright, moon paired—long shining over the ten thousand regions.
translations.idiomatic: the sun bright and the moon paired—long shining over the ten thousand regions.

sentences.zh: 朕欲躋世於乂安，爾其助予之德化，共禦亨嘉之運，益延昌熾之期。

translations.literal: We wish to place the age in governance and peace; you must assist our moral transformation, together facing the prosperous and excellent fortune, further extending the period of flourishing abundance.
translations.idiomatic: We wish to place the age in governance and peace; you must assist our moral transformation, together facing prosperous fortune and further extending the period of flourishing abundance.

sentences.zh: 勉爾徽音，聿修內治。

translations.literal: Exert your fine reputation and thereby cultivate inner rule.
translations.idiomatic: Exert your fine reputation and thereby cultivate inner rule.

sentences.zh: 」生皇子真金，二歲而夭。

translations.literal: " She bore the prince Jinjin, who died at two years.
translations.idiomatic: " She bore Prince Jinjin, who died at the age of two.

sentences.zh: 后性節儉，不妒忌，動以禮法自持。

translations.literal: The empress was by nature thrifty and not jealous, always holding herself with ritual and law.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was by nature thrifty and free of jealousy, always holding herself by ritual and law.

sentences.zh: 第二皇后奇氏素有寵，居興聖西宮，帝希幸東內。

translations.literal: The second empress Gi had long held favor, dwelling in the western palace of Xingsheng; the emperor rarely visited the eastern inner quarters.
translations.idiomatic: The second empress Gi had long held favor, dwelling in the western palace of Xingsheng; the emperor rarely visited the eastern inner quarters.

sentences.zh: 后左右以為言，后無幾微怨望意。

translations.literal: Those about the empress spoke of it to her, yet the empress had not the slightest trace of resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Those about the empress spoke of it to her, yet she showed not the slightest trace of resentment.

sentences.zh: 從帝時巡上京，次中道，帝遣內官傳旨，欲臨幸，后辭曰：「暮夜非至尊往來之時。

translations.literal: Following the emperor on tour to Shangdu, midway on the road the emperor sent an inner eunuch with an edict wishing to visit her; the empress declined, saying: "Nightfall is not the time for the utmost honored to come and go.
translations.idiomatic: Following the emperor on tour to Shangdu, midway on the road the emperor sent an inner eunuch with an edict wishing to visit her; the empress declined: "Nightfall is not the time for the Son of Heaven to come and go.

sentences.zh: 」內官往復者三，竟拒不納，帝益賢之。

translations.literal: " The inner eunuch went back and forth three times; she finally refused to admit him, and the emperor esteemed her all the more.
translations.idiomatic: " The inner eunuch went back and forth three times; she finally refused him entry, and the emperor esteemed her all the more.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗問后：「中政院所支錢糧，皆傳汝旨，汝還記之否？

translations.literal: The emperor once asked the empress: "The money and grain disbursed by the Central Administration all pass on your command—do you still remember them?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once asked the empress: "The money and grain disbursed by the Central Administration all pass on your command—do you still remember them?

sentences.zh: 」后對曰：「妾當用則支。

translations.literal: " The empress replied: "Your subject disburses when there is use.
translations.idiomatic: " The empress replied: "I disburse when there is need.

sentences.zh: 關防出入，必己選人司之，妾豈能盡記耶？

translations.literal: Passing in and out of the seal office must be managed by persons I myself select—how can your subject remember everything?
translations.idiomatic: Passing in and out of the seal office must be managed by persons I myself select—how could I remember everything?

sentences.zh: 」居坤德殿，終日端坐，未嘗妄逾戶閾。

translations.literal: " Dwelling in Kunde Hall, she sat upright all day and never rashly crossed the door-sill.
translations.idiomatic: " Dwelling in Kunde Hall, she sat upright all day and never rashly crossed the threshold.

sentences.zh: 至正二十五年八月崩，年四十二。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the twenty-fifth year of Zhizheng she died, age forty-two.
translations.idiomatic: She died in the eighth month of 1365, at the age of forty-two.

sentences.zh: 奇氏後見其所遺衣服弊壞，大笑曰：「正宮皇后，何至服此等衣耶！

translations.literal: Later when Gi saw the clothes she had left behind, worn and damaged, she laughed loudly and said: "The principal-palace empress—how could she wear clothes like these!
translations.idiomatic: Later when Gi saw the clothes she had left behind, worn and threadbare, she laughed and said: "The principal-palace empress—how could she wear clothes like these!

sentences.zh: 」其樸素可知。

translations.literal: " Her plain simplicity can be known from this.
translations.idiomatic: " Her plain simplicity can be known from this.

sentences.zh: 逾月，皇太子自冀寧歸，哭之甚哀。

translations.literal: After more than a month the crown prince returned from Jining and wept for her exceedingly.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a month the crown prince returned from Jining and wept for her exceedingly.

sentences.zh: 完者忽都皇后奇氏，高麗人，生皇太子愛猷識理達臘。

translations.literal: Empress Öljei Qudu Gi, a Korean, bore the crown prince Ayushiridara.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Öljei Qudu Gi, a Korean, bore Crown Prince Ayushiridara.

sentences.zh: 家微，用后貴，三世皆追封王爵。

translations.literal: Her family was humble; after the empress became honored, three generations were all posthumously ennobled as kings.
translations.idiomatic: Her family was humble; after she became empress, three generations were all posthumously ennobled as kings.

sentences.zh: 初，徽政院使禿滿叠兒進為宮女，主供茗飲，以事順帝。

translations.literal: At first the Huizheng Court commissioner Tumenjir presented her as a palace woman to serve tea; she attended Shundi.
translations.idiomatic: At first Huizheng Court Commissioner Tumenjir presented her as a palace woman to serve tea; she attended Shundi.

sentences.zh: 后性穎黠，日見寵幸。

translations.literal: The empress was clever and sharp and daily gained favor.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was clever and sharp and daily gained favor.

sentences.zh: 後答納失裏皇后方驕妒，數箠辱之。

translations.literal: Later Empress Danashirin was arrogant and jealous and often beat and humiliated her.
translations.idiomatic: Later Empress Danashirin was arrogant and jealous and often beat and humiliated her.

sentences.zh: 答納失裏既遇害，帝欲立之，丞相伯顏爭不可。

translations.literal: After Danashirin met with disaster, the emperor wished to establish Gi as empress; Chief Minister Bayan argued it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: After Danashirin met with disaster, the emperor wished to make Gi empress; Chief Minister Bayan argued it could not be done.

sentences.zh: 伯顏罷相，沙剌班遂請立為第二皇后，居興聖宮，改徽政院為資正院。

translations.literal: When Bayan was dismissed from office, Sharaben then requested establishing her as second empress; she dwelt in Xingsheng Palace and the Huizheng Court was changed to the Zizheng Court.
translations.idiomatic: When Bayan was dismissed, Sharaben requested establishing her as second empress; she dwelt in Xingsheng Palace and the Huizheng Court was changed to the Zizheng Court.

sentences.zh: 后無事，則取《女孝經》、史書，訪問歷代皇后之有賢行者為法。

translations.literal: When the empress had nothing to do she would take the "Classic of Filial Piety for Women" and historical books and inquire after empresses of successive ages who had worthy conduct to take as models.
translations.idiomatic: When idle she would take the Classic of Filial Piety for Women and historical books and inquire after empresses of successive ages who had shown worthy conduct, taking them as models.

sentences.zh: 四方貢獻，或有珍味，輒先遣使薦太廟，然后敢食。

translations.literal: When tribute from the four quarters had rare delicacies, she always first sent envoys to offer them at the Grand Temple and only then dared to eat.
translations.idiomatic: When tribute from the four quarters brought rare delicacies, she always first sent envoys to offer them at the Grand Temple and only then dared to eat.

sentences.zh: 至正十八年，京城大饑，后命官為粥食之。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Zhizheng there was great famine in the capital; the empress ordered officials to make gruel and feed the people.
translations.idiomatic: In 1358 there was great famine in the capital; the empress ordered officials to make gruel and feed the people.

sentences.zh: 又出金銀粟帛，命資正院使樸不花於京都十一門置冢，葬死者遺骼十餘萬，復命僧建水陸大會度之。

translations.literal: She also contributed gold, silver, grain, and cloth and ordered Zizheng Court Commissioner Puhua to set up burial mounds at the eleven gates of the capital, burying more than a hundred thousand skeletal remains of the dead, and again ordered monks to perform a great water-and-land assembly to deliver them.
translations.idiomatic: She also contributed gold, silver, grain, and cloth and ordered Zizheng Court Commissioner Puhua to set up burial mounds at the eleven gates of the capital, burying more than a hundred thousand skeletal remains, and ordered monks to perform a great water-and-land assembly for their deliverance.

sentences.zh: 時帝頗怠於政治，后與皇太子愛猷識理達臘遽謀內禪，遣樸不花諭意丞相太平，太平不答。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor was quite slack in government; the empress and Crown Prince Ayushiridara urgently plotted inner abdication and sent Puhua to convey their intent to Chief Minister Toqto'a; Toqto'a did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then quite slack in government; the empress and Crown Prince Ayushiridara urgently plotted inner abdication and sent Puhua to convey their intent to Chief Minister Toqto'a, who did not reply.

sentences.zh: 復召太平至宮，舉酒賜之，自申前請，太平依違而已，由是后與太子銜之。

translations.literal: They again summoned Toqto'a to the palace, raised a cup and bestowed it on him, personally stating the former request; Toqto'a was evasive only, and therefore the empress and crown prince harbored resentment against him.
translations.idiomatic: They again summoned Toqto'a to the palace, raised a cup and bestowed it on him, and personally stated the former request; Toqto'a was evasive only, and therefore the empress and crown prince harbored resentment against him.

sentences.zh: 而帝亦知后意，怒而疏之，兩月不見。

translations.literal: The emperor also knew the empress's intent, grew angry and estranged her, and for two months did not see her.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also knew the empress's intent, grew angry and estranged her, and for two months did not see her.

sentences.zh: 樸不花因后而寵幸，既被劾黜，后諷御史大夫佛家奴為之辯明。

translations.literal: Puhua because of the empress gained favor; after he was impeached and dismissed, the empress hinted that Censor-in-Chief Buddhanagu should argue on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Puhua gained favor through the empress; after he was impeached and dismissed, she hinted that Censor-in-Chief Buddhanagu should argue on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 佛家奴乃謀再劾樸不花，后知之，反嗾御史劾佛家奴，謫居潮河。

translations.literal: Buddhanagu then plotted to impeach Puhua again; the empress learned of it and in turn incited censors to impeach Buddhanagu, who was demoted to reside at Chaohe.
translations.idiomatic: Buddhanagu then plotted to impeach Puhua again; the empress learned of it and in turn incited censors to impeach Buddhanagu, who was demoted to Chaohe.

sentences.zh: 初，奇氏之族在高麗者，怙勢驕橫，高麗王怒，盡殺之。

translations.literal: At first Gi's clan in Korea, relying on power, were arrogant; the King of Korea was angry and killed them all.
translations.idiomatic: At first Gi's clan in Korea, relying on their power, were arrogant; the King of Korea was enraged and killed them all.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，后謂皇太子曰：「汝何不為我復讎耶？

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year the empress said to the crown prince: "Why do you not take revenge for me?
translations.idiomatic: In 1363 the empress said to the crown prince: "Why do you not take revenge for me?

sentences.zh: 」遂立高麗王族人留京師者為王，以奇族之子三寶奴為元子。

translations.literal: " Thereupon they established a member of the Korean royal clan remaining in the capital as king, with Gi's clansman Sanbaonu as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: " They established a member of the Korean royal clan remaining in the capital as king, with Gi's clansman Sanbaonu as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 遣同知樞密院事崔帖木兒為丞相，用兵一萬，並招倭兵，共往納之。

translations.literal: They dispatched Associate Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs Cui Temür as chief minister, with ten thousand troops, and also recruited Japanese troops, together going to install him.
translations.idiomatic: They dispatched Associate Commissioner Cui Temür as chief minister with ten thousand troops, also recruiting Japanese troops, together going to install him.

sentences.zh: 過鴨綠水，伏兵四起，乃大敗，余十七騎而還，后大慚。

translations.literal: Crossing the Yalu River, ambush troops rose on all sides; they were greatly defeated and only seventeen horsemen returned—the empress was deeply ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Crossing the Yalu River, ambush troops rose on all sides; they were greatly defeated and only seventeen horsemen returned—the empress was deeply ashamed.

sentences.zh: 二十四年七月，孛羅帖木兒稱兵犯闕，皇太子出奔冀寧，下令討孛羅帖木兒。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the twenty-fourth year Bolod Temür raised troops and violated the palace; the crown prince fled to Jining and issued orders to attack Bolod Temür.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of 1364 Bolod Temür raised troops and violated the palace; the crown prince fled to Jining and issued orders to attack him.

sentences.zh: 孛羅帖木兒怒，嗾監察御史武起宗言后外撓國政，奏帝宜遷后出於外，帝不答。

translations.literal: Bolod Temür was angry and incited Supervising Censor Wu Qizong to say the empress interfered externally in state government; he memorialized that the emperor should move the empress outside—the emperor did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Bolod Temür was angry and incited Supervising Censor Wu Qizong to say the empress interfered externally in government; he memorialized that the emperor should move her outside—the emperor did not reply.

sentences.zh: 二十五年三月，遂矯制幽於諸色總管府，令其黨姚伯顏不花守之。

translations.literal: In the third month of the twenty-fifth year he then forged an edict and confined her in the Office of the Various Commissaries, ordering his partisan Yao Bayanbuhua to guard her.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of 1365 he forged an edict and confined her in the Office of the Various Commissaries, ordering his partisan Yao Bayanbuhua to guard her.

sentences.zh: 四月庚寅，孛羅帖木兒逼后還宮，取印章，偽為后書召太子。

translations.literal: On the gengyin day of the fourth month Bolod Temür forced the empress back to the palace, took the seals, and falsely wrote in the empress's hand to summon the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengyin day of the fourth month Bolod Temür forced the empress back to the palace, took the seals, and forged a summons to the crown prince in her name.

sentences.zh: 后仍回幽所，后又數納美女於孛羅帖木兒，至百日，始還宮。

translations.literal: The empress still returned to confinement; she again several times presented beautiful women to Bolod Temür; after a hundred days she at last returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The empress still returned to confinement; she again several times presented beautiful women to Bolod Temür; after a hundred days she at last returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 及孛羅帖木兒死，召皇太子還京師，后傳旨令廓擴帖木兒以兵擁皇太子入城，欲脅帝禪位。

translations.literal: When Bolod Temür died, the crown prince was summoned back to the capital; the empress transmitted an edict ordering Köke Temür to lead troops and escort the crown prince into the city, intending to coerce the emperor to abdicate.
translations.idiomatic: When Bolod Temür died, the crown prince was summoned back to the capital; the empress transmitted an edict ordering Köke Temür to escort the crown prince into the city with troops, intending to coerce the emperor to abdicate.

sentences.zh: 廓擴帖木兒知其意，至京城三十里外，即遣軍還營，皇太子復銜之。

translations.literal: Köke Temür knew her intent; thirty li outside the capital he at once sent the army back to camp, and the crown prince again harbored resentment against him.
translations.idiomatic: Köke Temür knew her intent; thirty li outside the capital he sent the army back to camp, and the crown prince again harbored resentment against him.

sentences.zh: 事見《擴廓帖木兒傳》。

translations.literal: The matter is seen in the biography of Köke Temür.
